coverage.main: Read all eighteen pages of arXiv 2202.02215v6 (20 June 2023), Sections I-VIII, Figures 1-5, Tables I-II and references. Section VII.D discusses 'transferability' of generated driving scenarios across autonomous-vehicle policies conceptually, without experiments.
coverage.supplement: No appendix or supplement is included or linked. The IEEE T-ITS version of record was not retrieved; arXiv v6 is the latest version.
coverage.excluded_results: Figure 2 and Sections III-V classify prior scenario-generation methods; Table I compares datasets; Table II compares simulators; Section VI lists platforms; Sections VII-VIII discuss challenges. None reports an original numerical attack or transfer result.

f1.evidence: The paper is a methodological survey of safety-critical driving scenario generation with no original source/target model evaluation.

f2.evidence: No original transfer denominator exists to code.

f3.evidence: Scenario transferability is discussed conceptually; no source-success conditioning question arises.

f4.evidence: Tables compare datasets and simulators, not attack outcomes.

f5.evidence: Pixel-level and semantic attacks are mentioned in passing; no original perturbation budget applies. Not a claim of deficient reporting.

f6.evidence: No original transfer configuration exists for which artifacts could be sufficient or insufficient.

artifact_checks.result: Downloaded and hashed v6. The paper links no code or experimental supplement; referenced platforms such as SafeBench are separate works and were not treated as artifacts of this survey.

bounds_exclusion.reason: No original numerical attack rate or clean baseline is reported.

limitations: Retained in the frozen corpus with non-applicability reasons; report separately from ambiguous reporting.
Non-blind evidence audit; T-ITS version of record not inspected.
